When I approached the Sarojini Nagar Police Station to report this incident, the officers on duty refused to register an FIR and instead advised me to file a 'lost report' online. # Formal Complaint regarding theft of mobile phone at Sarojini Market

**To:** The Station House Officer, Sarojini Nagar Police Station Police Station (submit at the police station or on your state police portal)

Aapka phone Sarojini market mein chori hua hai aur police ne FIR likhne se mana kar diya hai. Is letter mein humne request ki hai ki FIR register ho kyunki aapke phone mein bank apps hain aur IMEI abhi tak block nahi hua hai. Aap ise police station mein submit karke stamped receipt zaroor lein.

```
To,
The Station House Officer
Sarojini Nagar Police Station Police Station


Date: 09 October 2026

Subject: Formal Complaint regarding theft of mobile phone at Sarojini Market

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to formally report the theft of my mobile phone, which occurred on 24 September at approximately 1 PM at Sarojini Market. When I approached the Sarojini Nagar Police Station to report this incident, the officers on duty refused to register an FIR and instead advised me to file a 'lost report' online. I am deeply concerned about this refusal. My mobile phone contains sensitive financial information, including active bank applications and UPI accounts. While I have already notified my bank and UPI provider regarding the theft to secure my accounts, I have not yet blocked the IMEI number of the device. Given the potential for unauthorized access and financial fraud, it is critical that an FIR is registered to initiate a proper investigation and to facilitate the necessary security measures. I request you to kindly register an FIR regarding this theft, provide me with a free copy of the same, and initiate an investigation to trace the device. ## Where to report, and if the police don't act
```
1. **National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in** (call 1930 · report on cybercrime.gov.in · call your bank to block the account/card) — Immediately — within hours if possible, so the money can be traced and frozen. Note the acknowledgement number and quote it in your police complaint. https://cybercrime.gov.in · 1930
2. **Station House Officer (SHO), Sarojini Nagar Police Station** (written complaint at the police station · e-FIR on your state police citizen portal where available) — Give your written complaint at the police station. For a cognizable offence the police must register an FIR; you can report at any police station (zero FIR) and you are entitled to a free copy. Get a signed and stamped receipt for your written complaint. · 112
3. **Superintendent of Police / Deputy Commissioner of Police** (complaint in writing by registered post or in person) — If the SHO refuses to register an FIR: send the substance of your complaint in writing to the SP/DCP (BNSS, 2023, s.173(4)). Keep the postal receipt.
4. **Judicial Magistrate** (application through a lawyer or the District Legal Services Authority (free if eligible)) — If the police still do not act: apply to the Magistrate to direct registration and investigation (BNSS, 2023, s.175(3)). https://nalsa.gov.in · 15100

_Information, not legal advice._
